# Zerro — full site content

> Zerro is a native macOS menu-bar utility that turns a screen recording and spoken
> instructions into a structured prompt for AI coding agents. Record it. Paste it.
> Zerro in between.

This file contains the full marketing-site content as Markdown, for AI tools that
want deep ingestion. Source: https://getzerro.app

---

## What is Zerro?

Zerro is a native macOS menu-bar utility that turns a screen recording and spoken
instructions into a structured prompt for AI coding agents. You frame a region of
your screen, dictate what you want in plain language, and Zerro returns a Markdown
prompt ready to paste into Cursor, Windsurf, v0, or any agent you already use.

Processing is local-first: audio isolation and frame downsampling happen on your
machine before a single API call turns the recording into a prompt. You bring your
own OpenAI and Gemini keys, stored in the macOS Keychain — there are no servers in
the middle handling your data, and no account required.

Think of it as voice dictation for your codebase: instead of plain text, you get a
structured prompt. There's no new app to learn; the whole flow runs from the menu bar.

---

## How it works — Record. Speak. Copy.

1. **Select a region.** Hit the hotkey, drag to frame the part of your screen you
   want the agent to see. Native macOS crosshair, no window switching.
2. **Dictate what you want.** Talk it through like you'd explain it to a teammate.
   Point at things, change your mind, ramble. Zerro records up to 3 minutes.
3. **Zerro processes locally.** Audio gets isolated and frames get downsampled on
   your machine. Then a single API call turns it into a structured prompt.
4. **Paste the prompt.** A Markdown prompt lands on your clipboard, ready to drop
   into Cursor, Windsurf, v0, or wherever you ship from.

The prompt writes itself — you get a structured Markdown prompt with clear sections
(such as Context, Current State, and Request) rather than a raw transcript.

---

## Built right — native, local-first, no surprises

Zerro is built the way you'd build it if it were your tool.

- **Native Swift & SwiftUI.** A real menu-bar app, built on ScreenCaptureKit. Not
  an Electron tab pretending to be a Mac app.
- **Local-first processing.** Audio isolation and frame downsampling happen on your
  machine before anything leaves it.
- **Bring your own keys.** Your OpenAI and Gemini keys, stored in macOS Keychain.
  No servers handling your data.
- **Cost-bounded by design.** A 3-minute hard cap on every recording keeps each
  request fast, cheap, and predictable.
- **Signed & notarized.** Distributed direct as a code-signed .dmg. macOS
  Gatekeeper will not complain.
- **Sparkle auto-updates.** Updates ship through Sparkle, the standard for indie
  Mac apps. You stay current without thinking about it.

## How it compares

Dictation tools give you text. Screen recorders give you a video. Zerro gives your
agent a prompt. This comparison reflects Zerro's positioning; competitor
capabilities change over time, so check each product for current details.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Primary input | Screen + voice | Voice | Screen + voice |
| Output | Structured prompt | Dictated text | Video link |
| Built for AI coding agents | Yes | No | No |
| Local-first processing | Yes | No | No |
| Bring your own API keys | Yes | No | No |
| Native macOS app | Yes | Yes | No |
| Pricing model | One-time ($39) | Subscription | Subscription |

## The shift — now we're talking

The keyboard was never the point — it was just the only interface we had. As agents
get better at acting on what you actually mean, typing out every instruction by hand
starts to feel like the bottleneck it always was.

You think faster than you type. You talk faster than you think. Voice closes that
gap — and dictation is becoming the default. You speak nearly 4× faster than you
type. Zerro is built for that future: less typing, more talking.

## FAQ

**What is Zerro?**
Zerro is a native macOS menu-bar app that records a region of your screen and your
voice, then returns a structured Markdown prompt ready to paste into an AI coding
agent like Cursor, Windsurf, or v0.

**Does Zerro work with Cursor?**
Yes. Zerro puts a structured Markdown prompt on your clipboard, so it works with
Cursor, Windsurf, v0, or any tool that takes a text prompt. It isn't tied to a
single agent.

**Can Zerro replace Wispr Flow?**
They solve different problems. Wispr Flow is general voice dictation that types text
for you. Zerro is purpose-built for coding agents: it captures your screen alongside
your voice and returns a structured prompt, not plain dictated text.

**How much does Zerro cost?**
Zerro is a one-time purchase of $39 for the BYOK plan, which includes all features
and future updates. A Managed plan at $12/month — where Zerro handles token usage
and no API keys are required — is coming soon.

**Is my data private?**
Yes. Audio isolation and frame downsampling run locally on your Mac before anything
leaves it. Zerro uses your own OpenAI and Gemini keys, stored in the macOS Keychain,
so there are no Zerro servers handling your recordings.

**Does Zerro need an account?**
No. The BYOK plan requires no account and no subscription. You bring your own API
keys and pay once.

**How long can a recording be?**
Each recording is capped at 3 minutes. The hard cap keeps every request fast, cheap,
and predictable.
